Uttar Pradesh has a very large population and a high population growth rate. From 1991 to 2001 its population increased by over 26 per cent.[[127]](#cite_note-population-127) It is the [most populous state in India](/wiki/List_of_states_and_union_territories_of_India_by_population "List of states and union territories of India by population"), with 199,581,477 people on 1 March 2011.[[128]](#cite_note-autogenerated7-128) The state contributes to 16.2 per cent of India's population. As of 2021, the estimated population of the state is around 240 million people.[[129]](#cite_note-Estimated_2021-129) The population density is 828 people per square kilometre, making it one of the most densely populated [states](/wiki/States_and_territories_of_India "States and territories of India") in the country.[[130]](#cite_note-Statistics-130) It has the largest [scheduled caste](/wiki/Scheduled_caste "Scheduled caste") population, making up 23% of the state's population, whereas [scheduled tribes](/wiki/List_of_Scheduled_Tribes_in_India "List of Scheduled Tribes in India") are less than 1 per cent of the total population.[[131]](#cite_note-Tribe-131)[[132]](#cite_note-Indigenous-132)

fanoutqa_024889.t: Crocus :: Taxonomy :: Similarly named species :: chunk_0015
fanoutqa_024889.x:
Crocus :: Taxonomy :: Similarly named species :: chunk_0015
Some crocus species, known as "autumn crocus", flower in late summer and autumn, during (autumnal) rains, after summer's heat and drought. The name **autumn crocus** is also often used as a common name for *[Colchicum](/wiki/Colchicum "Colchicum")*,[[68]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWyman1986-70) which is not a true crocus but in its own family ([Colchicaceae](/wiki/Colchicaceae "Colchicaceae")) in the lily order [Liliales](/wiki/Liliales "Liliales"). The plants are toxic, but have medicinal uses. *Colchicum* are also known as **meadow saffron**, though true [saffron](/wiki/Saffron "Saffron") is not toxic.[[69]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGBIF2022-71) *Crocus* species have three stamens while *Colchicum* species have six;[[70]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEArmitage2008278-72) crocus have one style, while *Colchicum* have three.[[71]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBowles1985154-73)[[10]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMabberley1997-10)

Some [Pulsatilla](/wiki/Pulsatilla "Pulsatilla") species are also called "prairie crocus" (previously *[Anemone patens](/wiki/Pulsatilla_patens "Pulsatilla patens"))* or "wild crocus", but they belong to the buttercup family ([Ranunculaceae](/wiki/Ranunculaceae "Ranunculaceae")).[[72]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTERunkelRoosa20097-74)[[73]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESkelly1994-75) Pulsatilla species, which are commonly called pasqueflowers, unlike crocuses have [rhizomes](/wiki/Rhizome "Rhizome"), the foliage is covered with long soft hairs, and the flowers are produced on above-ground stems.[[74]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWencaiBartholomew2004-76)[[75]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEArmitage2008843-77)

The [Boston Celtics](/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics") have won the most championships of any NBA team. Shown are the championship banners hanging in their home arena, [TD Garden](/wiki/TD_Garden "TD Garden").

The most recent champions are the [Oklahoma City Thunder](/wiki/Oklahoma_City_Thunder "Oklahoma City Thunder"), who won their first championship since [relocating from Seattle](/wiki/Seattle_SuperSonics_relocation_to_Oklahoma_City "Seattle SuperSonics relocation to Oklahoma City") in 2008, and their first since [1979](/wiki/1979_NBA_Finals "1979 NBA Finals") as the [Seattle SuperSonics](/wiki/Seattle_SuperSonics "Seattle SuperSonics"). The [Boston Celtics](/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics") have won the most championships of any team in the league at 18.[[5]](#cite_note-5) As of 2025, the Eastern champions have a 41–38 advantage in NBA titles over the Western champions. The [1949–50 Minneapolis Lakers](/wiki/1949%E2%80%9350_Minneapolis_Lakers_season "1949–50 Minneapolis Lakers season"), who won the [NBA Finals](/wiki/1950_NBA_Finals "1950 NBA Finals"), are counted in the Eastern versus Western champions record as they played that sole season in the Central Division before returning to the Western Division.

[John Roberts](/wiki/John_Roberts "John Roberts") giving testimony before the Senate Judiciary Committee during the [2005 hearings on his nomination](/wiki/John_Roberts_Supreme_Court_nomination#Confirmation_hearings "John Roberts Supreme Court nomination") to be chief justice

Article II, Section 2, Clause 2 of the [United States Constitution](/wiki/United_States_Constitution "United States Constitution"), known as the [Appointments Clause](/wiki/Appointments_Clause "Appointments Clause"), empowers the [president](/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") to nominate and, with the confirmation ([advice and consent](/wiki/Advice_and_consent "Advice and consent")) of the United States Senate, to appoint public [officials](/wiki/Official "Official"), including justices of the Supreme Court. This clause is one example of the system of checks and balances inherent in the Constitution. The president has the [plenary power](/wiki/Plenary_power "Plenary power") to nominate, while the Senate possesses the plenary power to reject or confirm the nominee. The Constitution sets no qualifications for service as a justice, such as age, citizenship, residence or prior judicial experience, thus a president may nominate anyone to serve, and the Senate may not set any qualifications or otherwise limit who the president can choose.[[83]](#cite_note-83) Nonetheless, the Senate may deny confirmation to a candidate that

The Ioniq 5 N was introduced on 14 July 2023 during the [Goodwood Festival of Speed](/wiki/Goodwood_Festival_of_Speed "Goodwood Festival of Speed"). The variant is the top-of-the-line model, marketed under the [Hyundai N](/wiki/Hyundai_N "Hyundai N") performance sub-brand.[[27]](#cite_note-27)[[28]](#cite_note-28)

The exterior changes include a revised front end with larger air intakes, with additional air curtains and air flaps for improved cooling. The rear portion gained a rear wiper, wing-type spoiler integrated with a triangular third brake light, and a rear [diffuser](/wiki/Diffuser_(automotive) "Diffuser (automotive)"). With extended wheel arches and wider [track](/wiki/Axle_track "Axle track"), the Ioniq 5 N is 50 mm (2.0 in) wider than the standard model and also 20 mm (0.8 in) lower.[[29]](#cite_note-:1-29) The larger front motor and front external speaker mean the Ioniq 5 N loses the front boot / trunk present in other Ioniq models.

The [body in white](/wiki/Body_in_white "Body in white") structure of the Ioniq 5 N gains 42 additional welding points and 2.1 m (83 in) of additional adhesives for improved rigidity. The motor and battery mountings were also reinforced, while the [subframes](/wiki/Subframe "Subframe") were enhanced for lateral rigidity. Its power steering has a higher ratio and improved torque feedback.

The vehicle is equipped with two electric motors, providing a total of 448 kW (609 PS; 601 hp) and 740 N⋅m (75.5 kg⋅m; 546 lb⋅ft) of torque. Hyundai equipped the Ioniq 5 N with an N Grin Boost mode, allowing a maximum output of 478 kW (650 PS; 641 hp) and 770 N⋅m (78.5 kg⋅m; 568 lb⋅ft) of torque being released for 10 seconds. Hyundai claimed a 0–100 km/h (0–62 mph) acceleration figure of 3.5 seconds, or 3.4 seconds with launch control or with N Grin Boost mode activated. fanoutqa_024377.x:
Big Sur :: Flora and fauna :: Southern limit of redwood trees :: chunk_0042
Main article: [Sequoia sempervirens](/wiki/Sequoia_sempervirens "Sequoia sempervirens")

The high coastal mountains trap moisture from the clouds: fog in summer, rain, and snow in winter creating a favorable environment for the [coast redwood](/wiki/Sequoia_sempervirens "Sequoia sempervirens") (*Sequoia sempervirens*) trees found in the Big Sur region. They are found near the ocean in canyon bottoms or inland canyons alongside creeks and in other areas that meet its requirements for cooler temperatures and moisture. Due to drier conditions, trees in the Big Sur region only grow about 200 feet (61 m) tall, smaller than specimens found to the north.[[196]](#cite_note-ipfw-196)

The redwood trees in Big Sur are the remnant of much larger groves. Many old-growth trees were cut by the Ventana Power Company which operated a sawmill near present-day Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park from the late 1800s through 1906 when its operations were bankrupted by the [1906 San Francisco earthquake](/wiki/1906_San_Francisco_earthquake "1906 San Francisco earthquake"). When John and Florence Pfeiffer opened Pfeiffer's Ranch Resort in 1910, they built guest cabins from lumber cut using the mill. The mill was resurrected when Highway 1 was constructed during the 1920s. It supplied lumber for housing built for workers.[[197]](#cite_note-197)[[198]](#cite_note-pelican_lodge-198)

While many trees were harvested, several inaccessible locations were never logged. A large grove of trees is found along the north fork of the Little Sur River. [William Randolph Hearst](/wiki/William_Randolph_Hearst "William Randolph Hearst") was interested in preserving the uncut redwood forest, and on November 18, 1921, he purchased about 1,445 acres (585 ha) from the Eberhard and Kron Tanning Company of Santa Cruz for about $50,000. [DeDe Dorsey](/wiki/DeDe_Dorsey "DeDe Dorsey") was placed on [injured reserve](/wiki/Injured_reserve "Injured reserve") and [Chris Perry](/wiki/Chris_Perry_(American_football) "Chris Perry (American football)") was the starter. Benson's season began in a loss to the [Dallas Cowboys](/wiki/Dallas_Cowboys "Dallas Cowboys"), rushing 10 times for 30 yards. He became the starting back for the Bengals in Week 7 against the [Pittsburgh Steelers](/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers "Pittsburgh Steelers").[[21]](#cite_note-21) Benson rushed 14 times for 52 yards in his first career start as a Bengal. In the following 35–6 loss to the [Houston Texans](/wiki/Houston_Texans "Houston Texans"), he totaled 49 yards on 13 carries and had two receptions for 20 yards. The Bengals picked up their first victory of the season in a 21–19 game against the [Jacksonville Jaguars](/wiki/Jacksonville_Jaguars "Jacksonville Jaguars"), with Benson carrying 24 times for 104 yards and a touchdown. Benson hit his stride in the Bengals' three-game winning streak at the end of the season, gashing the [Washington Redskins](/wiki/Washington_Redskins "Washington Redskins") in week 15 with 161 yards from scrimmage, including 88 yards receiving (79 of which came on a screen pass). In week 16, Benson dominated the [Cleveland Browns](/wiki/Cleveland_Browns "Cleveland Browns"), rushing for 171 yards. In the final game of the season against the [Kansas City Chiefs](/wiki/Kansas_City_Chiefs "Kansas City Chiefs"), Benson had 111 yards on 25 carries. In the twelve games he was active during the 2008 season, Benson had 932 yards from scrimmage: 747 rushing and 185 receiving.

In May 1828, Taylor was called back to action, commanding [Fort Snelling](/wiki/Fort_Snelling "Fort Snelling") in [Michigan Territory](/wiki/Michigan_Territory "Michigan Territory") (now [Minnesota](/wiki/Minnesota "Minnesota")) on the [Upper Mississippi River](/wiki/Upper_Mississippi_River "Upper Mississippi River") for a year, and then nearby [Fort Crawford](/wiki/Fort_Crawford "Fort Crawford"), also in the Michigan Territory (now [Wisconsin](/wiki/Wisconsin "Wisconsin")), in order to rebuild the previous fort, which had heavily damaged by a flood, for a year. After some time on furlough, spent expanding his landholdings, Taylor was promoted to colonel of the [1st Infantry Regiment](/wiki/1st_Infantry_Regiment_(United_States) "1st Infantry Regiment (United States)") in April 1832, when the [Black Hawk War](/wiki/Black_Hawk_War "Black Hawk War") was beginning in the West.[[57]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBauer198547–49-58)[[58]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHamilton194177–82-59) Taylor campaigned under General [Henry Atkinson](/wiki/Henry_Atkinson_(soldier) "Henry Atkinson (soldier)") to pursue and later defend against Chief [Black Hawk](/wiki/Black_Hawk_(Sauk_leader) "Black Hawk (Sauk leader)")'s forces throughout the summer. The end of the war in August 1832 signaled the final Indian resistance to U.S. expansion in the area.[[59]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBauer198559–65-60)[[60]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHamilton194183–99-61)

During this period, Taylor opposed the courtship of his 17-year-old daughter Sarah Knox Taylor with Lieutenant Jefferson Davis, the future [President of the Confederate States of America](/wiki/President_of_the_Confederate_States_of_America "President of the Confederate States of America"). He respected Davis but did not wish his daughter to become a military wife, as he knew it was a hard life for families. Søren Kirkegaard, existentialist philosopher considered one of the most important figures of the [Danish Golden Age](/wiki/Danish_Golden_Age "Danish Golden Age")[[285]](#cite_note-300)

The first known Danish literature is myths and [folklore](/wiki/Danish_folklore "Danish folklore") from the 10th and 11th century. [Saxo Grammaticus](/wiki/Saxo_Grammaticus "Saxo Grammaticus"), normally considered the first Danish writer, worked on a chronicle of [Danish history](/wiki/History_of_Denmark "History of Denmark") (*[Gesta Danorum](/wiki/Gesta_Danorum "Gesta Danorum")*). Very little is known of other Danish literature from the [Middle Ages](/wiki/Middle_Ages "Middle Ages"). With the [Age of Enlightenment](/wiki/Age_of_Enlightenment "Age of Enlightenment") came [Ludvig Holberg](/wiki/Ludvig_Holberg "Ludvig Holberg") whose comedy plays are still being performed.

In the late 19th century, literature was seen as a way to influence society. Known as the [Modern Breakthrough](/wiki/Modern_Breakthrough "Modern Breakthrough"), this movement was championed by [Georg Brandes](/wiki/Georg_Brandes "Georg Brandes"), [Henrik Pontoppidan](/wiki/Henrik_Pontoppidan "Henrik Pontoppidan")

The nomadic Inuit were traditionally [shamanistic](/wiki/Shamanism "Shamanism"), with a well-developed [Inuit religion](/wiki/Inuit_religion "Inuit religion") primarily concerned with appeasing a vengeful and [fingerless sea goddess](/wiki/Sedna_(mythology) "Sedna (mythology)") called Sedna who controlled the success of the [seal](/wiki/Seal_hunting "Seal hunting") and [whale hunts](/wiki/Whaling "Whaling").[[220]](#cite_note-227) The first [Norse colonists](/wiki/Norse_colonization_of_Greenland "Norse colonization of Greenland") worshipped the [Norse gods](/wiki/Norse_religion "Norse religion"), but Leif Erikson was converted to Christianity by King [Olaf Trygvesson](/wiki/Olaf_Trygvesson "Olaf Trygvesson") on a trip to Norway in 999 and sent missionaries back to Greenland. These swiftly established 16 parishes, some monasteries, and a bishopric at [Garðar](/wiki/Gar%C3%B0ar,_Greenland "Garðar, Greenland").

Rediscovering these colonists and spreading ideas of the [Protestant Reformation](/wiki/Reformation_in_Denmark%E2%80%93Norway_and_Holstein "Reformation in Denmark–Norway and Holstein") among them was one of the primary reasons for the [Danish recolonization](/wiki/Danish_colonization_of_the_Americas "Danish colonization of the Americas") in the 18th century.
